message.reasoning_content:
The kernel looks correct: in-place state update with aliasing issue? STATE and OUT alias. For r < L-K it reads STATE[b, r+K] which may already have been written by another program. In-place overlapping copy — hazard! Rows shift down by K, so writing row r overwrites data later needed... Actually with aliasing, program writing OUT row r may clobber STATE row r+K before it's read? Since output = state (same storage), and reads of row r+K can happen after writes to row r if programs execute out of order. This is a race. The contract says "Do not assume distinct pointer names imply distinct storage: inspect the arguments passed by run." So this is likely a bug: aliasing in-place shift is unsafe unless handled. Also reading row r+K where r+K > r? Writer writes row r (lower index), reader reads row r+K (higher index). Program order: blocks process index ranges in increasing order; block i reads indices around block i's range + K rows ahead. A block with lower index writes rows that earlier blocks... Actually a block writes its own index range; reads rows K ahead. If block j runs before block i (j<i), block j writes lower rows that no one needs (already processed? no). Race: block j writes row r; later block i reads row r+K which is written by block j' writing row r+K when r' = r+K. Writing row r+K happens in block whose range covers r+K, a higher block that may run before block j reads it? Block j (covering rows near r) reads row r+K which block j+k (covering row r+K) writes. If the higher block runs first, it clobbers state at row r+K before block j reads it → wrong data. This is a real race. Test it.
